page.layout: One page of text, verse set in one block, then a signature line "G. Buchananus." at right, and a gathering mark "III," at the lower right.

l.i: Carnifices, ferre ad manes solatia rara
Mortis, apud suam vere iactare Megaram,
Quod qui ne fieret quisquam te nequior alter
Certaris: tamen vnum inter tot sæua patraris
Dignum laude nefas, quod te confumpferis ipse
Dente tuo. Neque enim confueta piacula tanto
Sufficiunt sceleru̅ cumulo: nec more decebat
Humano finire dies, quum viceris omnem
Flagitijs famam, rabiem feritate ferarum,
Et spem quo possit venturo demferis ævo[?]
Nequitiam superare tuam, nec fœdior alter
Viueret in terris qui te demitteret Orco,
Orco qui tetri iamdudum exercet Auerni
Omnia monstra, tuis qui cuncta ergastula pœnis
Inuigilare facit, sceleram ut portenta nouorum
Supplicijs frænare nouis queat: ut breue tempus
Si tibi sit vacuum tormentis, qui modo terras
Miscueris tanta cum seditione tumultu,
Cogere ne possis bella ad ciuilia manes.
At tu diffidijs iam pene extincta nefandis,
Si fax diffidij pereat, dehinc, Gallia, gaude:
Nam simul ac terris tetrum dimisus ad Orcum
Carolus abscedet Furiarum agitante flagello,
Incolet incultas iterum pax aurea terras.

page.notes: Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout. Doubtful readings: "ævo" (possibly "auo") in line 9 of the first stanza, and the word after "sæua" in the second line of the first stanza, which is difficult to read and may be "sæua" or "fæua". "Sufficiunt sceleru̅" is printed as "sceelerum" with a macron-like abbreviation and is shown here as "sceleru̅" — check. The verse is printed as one unbroken block with no stanza breaks, so it is given as one paragraph per printed section.
